result:
No — don't cut production moderation over this week based on vendor marketing alone. "99.9% accuracy" and "SOC2 compliant" are unverified claims from a sales page (case studies are cherry-picked, and "SOC2 compliant" isn't the same as having passed a Type II audit — ask for the actual report and check the trust services criteria in scope), and moderation failures have real downstream harm (illegal content getting through, wrongful takedowns, legal/brand exposure) that you can't undo after the fact.

The tradeoff is cost savings now vs. the risk of unvalidated failure modes on your actual content mix — startups' claimed accuracy rarely transfers cleanly to a new domain. Before switching, I'd want: (1) a shadow/parallel run against your current pipeline on real traffic to compare precision/recall on your labeled edge cases, (2) the signed SOC2 report and DPA reviewed (especially if it processes user content/PII), and (3) a rollback plan if it goes live. That's a 1-2 week validation effort, not a blocker to eventually switching if the pricing is genuinely better.
